purpose: Reuse the existing Massive fetcher as a standalone Ubuntu tool for the existing ticker archive.
objective: Complete and publish the source-only development checkpoint, then let Spark own planning for subsequent development.

evidence: All six Python modules compiled and imported with HTTP blocked.
The existing verifier is read-only and the roster check reports physical endpoints without qualifying continuous coverage.
findings: The legacy source is pinned and the code is ready for a development checkpoint.
Exact parity with the incumbent maintainer revision is unverified.
The legacy ticker-level resume marker is not bound to a specific plan.

next_steps.action: Compare exact incumbent source when B02 provides a source-only snapshot.

spark_review.published_state_readback: Verified state.json and AGENTS.md on the development branch.

maintainer_comparison.finding: The archived owner implementation binds admission to inventory and index digests, and checks fulfillment against the qualified published partition. The standalone fetcher and verifier rely on ticker-only marker existence within a manually chosen staging directory.
maintainer_comparison.decision: Use the SHA-256 of the exact trusted plan bytes to scope the standalone staging directory in both entry points. Keep legacy directories intact and treat their unbound markers as unverified for new plans. Preserve owner admission and publication responsibilities.
maintainer_comparison.validation: Use an offline fixture with two different plans for the same ticker, plus a repeat of the same plan. Only the identical plan may reuse its completion marker. Confirm the verifier cannot treat old unbound markers as completed for the new plan.

plan_scoped_staging.evidence: Identical-plan resume, different-plan isolation and preservation of legacy markers passed offline.
